About the role

We are looking for a Senior Newbuilding Manager to take commercial ownership of complex newbuilding and vessel investment projects across their full lifecycle, from initial business case and market engagement through contracting, construction and delivery.

This is a senior commercial role requiring strong judgement, negotiation capability and the ability to navigate high-value, complex investment decisions in a global environment. You will work closely with Fleet Technology, Network Strategy, Chartering, Vessel Portfolio Management, Finance, Treasury, Legal and other key functions to ensure projects deliver the right balance of commercial value, contractual protection, technical requirements and long-term value.

Beyond individual newbuilding projects, you will provide senior commercial capacity across the wider tonnage agenda, supporting transactions such as sale and purchase (SnP), purchase options, sale and leaseback arrangements, newbuild for time charter and contract amendments.

Key responsibilities

• Drive the commercial development, procurement and execution of assigned newbuilding and vessel investment projects, from business case through tendering, contracting, construction and delivery.

• Lead or contribute to investment business cases covering vessel specification, timing, commercial structure, risk, CAPEX, cash flows and total cost of ownership.

• Lead or support shipyard engagements, tender processes, bid evaluations and negotiations of Letters of Intent (LOIs) and Shipbuilding Contracts, in close collaboration with Legal, Fleet Technology and Finance.

• Lead commercial yard due diligence and counterparty assessments, including financial strength, risk and compliance, together with Finance, Treasury and Compliance.

• Act as the commercial contract owner throughout the project lifecycle, managing contractual milestones, payments, guarantees, options, claims and amendments.

• Coordinate cross-functional project teams and ensure high-quality, timely governance submissions, decision papers and management reporting.

• Provide flexible senior commercial capacity across the wider tonnage portfolio during peak periods, including SnP transactions, purchase options, sale and leaseback projects, newbuild for time charter and contractual amendments.

• Monitor shipyard capacity, pricing, market dynamics and competitor activity, translating market intelligence into actionable commercial analysis and recommendations.

• Build and maintain strong relationships with key shipyards, shipbrokers, OEMs, advisers and internal stakeholders.

• Contribute to consistent commercial processes, knowledge sharing and lessons learned across the Newbuilding team.

• Work closely with fellow Senior Newbuilding Managers, providing support and project coverage as portfolio priorities and workloads evolve.

• Identify and escalate material commercial exposures and decisions outside agreed mandate to the Head of Newbuilding, while maintaining ownership and momentum of agreed workstreams through completion.

Who we are looking for

You are a commercially strong shipping professional who can combine strategic thinking with hands-on execution. You are comfortable taking ownership of significant commercial commitments, challenging assumptions and navigating complex negotiations involving multiple internal and external stakeholders.

You bring:

• Significant commercial experience within shipping, vessel investment, newbuilding, sale and purchase, or a comparable capital-intensive industry.

• Proven experience leading complex commercial negotiations and managing high-value contractual commitments within defined mandates.

• Strong commercial judgement and the ability to balance price, vessel specification, delivery schedule, contractual risk and long-term value.

• Experience developing investment cases and translating complex commercial considerations into clear recommendations for senior management.

• A strong track record in tendering and contracting, combined with a solid understanding of key financial indicators including CAPEX, cash flows and total cost of ownership.

• The ability to manage several complex projects simultaneously and respond effectively to changing priorities and periods of high workload.

• Strong stakeholder management skills and experience working across multiple functions in a global, matrix organisation.

• Excellent communication skills, with the ability to influence and engage confidently at senior levels.

• A good understanding of vessel specifications and maritime technology.

• Experience working with Asian shipyards is considered a strong advantage.

• A high degree of ownership, commercial integrity and attention to detail.

What success looks like

Success in this role will be measured through:

• Commercial value and contractual protection secured across assigned investments and projects.

• Quality and timeliness of investment recommendations, decision papers and governance submissions.

• Delivery within approved cost, schedule, mandate and contractual parameters.

• Effective management of commercial risks, options, milestones and contractual deadlines.

• Ability to flex across projects and transactions as portfolio priorities change.

• Strength and quality of relationships with strategic shipyards and contribution to the continued development of the shipyard supply base.

You will play an important role in ensuring that major vessel investments are commercially robust, well governed and positioned to create long-term value, while strengthening our ability to engage strategically with the global shipyard market.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral researcher in quantitative genetics and genomics with a focus on inbreeding depression and genetic diversity management

jobs.description:
The Center for Quantitative Genetics and Genomics (QGG) at Aarhus University, Denmark, invites applications for an exciting two-year postdoctoral position in the field of quantitative genetics and genomics applied to inbreeding management in livestock populations. The primary focus of this position is to investigate the genetic bases of inbreeding depression in dairy cattle.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a two-year position starting on 1 April 2027, or as soon as possible. 

Job description
This is an opportunity to integrate a top research environment and contribute to advancing the state of the art in inbreeding management, while working within a collaborative project involving key industry partners.

The overarching objective of the project is to quantify the impact of inbreeding depression load on economically important traits in dairy cattle breeds and to investigate whether recessive variants contributing to inbreeding depression segregate in genomic regions experiencing rapid accumulation of inbreeding. Particular attention will be given to regions surrounding monogenetic traits (e.g. polled locus, milk caseins) which have been subjected to strong selection pressure in recent years.

You will apply state-of-the-art quantitative genetic and genomic modelling approaches to evaluate the effect of inbreeding depression on a broad range of production and functional traits recorded in dairy cattle populations. To support these analyses, you will have access to extensive databases containing phenotypic records routinely collected on farm, as well as large-scale pedigree and SNP genomic datasets currently used in genomic evaluations. High-density SNP genotyping and whole-genome sequence data will also be available to search for causal variants and more finely describe the genetic architecture of inbreeding depression in dairy cattle. Ultimately, the project aims to incorporate these findings into practical mating software readily available to dairy farmers. Therefore, these activities will be carried out in close collaboration with industry partners to ensure practical implementation in the field. 

Within this position, the successful candidate will also have the opportunity to contribute to other research projects related to genetic diversity management and quantitative trait modelling across other livestock species. 

Your profile
• A Ph.D. in Quantitative Genetics, Population Genetics or similar.
• Good programming skills (R, Python or Julia)
• Experience in the use of software to estimate variance components is a plus (e.g. DMU, BLUPF90 or similar) 
• A team player and a good communicator
• A good track record of publication in international peer-reviewed journals
• Fluent in English (written and spoken)
Who we are
The Center for Quantitative Genetics and Genomics (QGG) is a major center for research and education in quantitative genetics and genomics at Aarhus University (http://www.qgg.au.dk/en). We conduct basic and applied research in animal, plant, and human genetics. Our focus areas include quantitative genetics, artificial intelligence applied to agriculture and medicine, population genetics, and integrative genomics. Research within QGG is characterized by a very close synergy between method development and application on practical problems across species, in collaboration with industry partners. QGG is an international research center with about 70 employees and visiting researchers from over 15 nations. QGG works in teams and strives for an excellent working environment, in which we value self-leadership, open communication, and commitment to diversity and inclusion.

What we offer
The successful candidate will be offered: 

• An interdisciplinary environment, in which the candidate will be able to exchange across disciplines and diverse applications (livestock, plants and biomedicine).
• An international research environment characterized by collaboration, professionalism, commitment to diversity and inclusion.
• Computational resources, including access to the GenomeDK high-performance computing cluster.
• A healthy work-life balance.
Place of work and area of employment 

The primary place of work is C. F. Møllers Allé 3, 8000, Aarhus C (Denmark).

Contact information
For further information, please contact Tenure-Track Assistant Professor Alban Bouquet, +45 2070 2677, alban.bouquet@qgg.au.dk
Associate Professor Zexi Cai, +45 8715 7928, zexi.cai@qgg.au.dk

Application procedure

Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship in causality and machine learning for treatment decisions, jointly at the Pioneer Centre for AI and the Pioneer Centre for SMARTBiomed

jobs.description:
Department of Mathematical Sciences, Faculty of SCIENCE, University of Copenhagen  The Department of Mathematical Sciences (MATH) invites applications for a PhD fellowship in causality and machine learning for treatment decisions. The fellowship is shared between the Pioneer Centre for AI and the Pioneer Centre for SMARTBiomed and is advertised at the Faculty of Science together with a three-year assistant professor position in causal inference at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences.

  The start date is 1 April 2027 or as soon as possible.  We are willing to accommodate the successful candidate’s situation, and the exact date is a matter of agreement.

  The setup: one project, two centres  You will be supervised by Sebastian Weichwald (Associate Professor at MATH, Copenhagen Causality Lab, and causality co-lead at the Pioneer Centre for AI) and Erin Gabriel (Professor at the Department of Public Health, causality theme lead and co-director of SMARTBiomed), and work closely with the assistant professor hired at Public Health also working jointly at the two centers, so that the link between the centres runs through daily work, not only meetings.

  Causal inference is a theme both centres share and approach from two sides. This position is for someone who wants both.

  About the centres: The Pioneer Centre for AI (https://www.aicentre.dk/), hosted by the Department of Computer Science with partners across Danish universities, does fundamental AI research. The Pioneer Centre for SMARTBiomed (https://smartbiomed.dk/) develops statistical and computational methods for large-scale biomedical data to improve the treatment and prevention of disease.

  The project  In diabetes management, continuous glucose monitoring is a high-frequency biomarker that is often used in treatment decisions. Given the huge amount of information summaries must be used; differences in summaries can lead to different decisions from the same raw data.  Treatment and prevention decisions increasingly rest on high-dimensional or high-frequency patient data such as biomarkers, wearable-device streams, omics profiles and longitudinal health records. In practice these are reduced to scores, coarser summaries, learned representations or patient states before a decision is made. The project asks when such a reduced representation still supports choosing between interventions, what is lost when it does not, and how representations can be learned with the decision in mind. It starts with the decision and works backwards to the measurements, transformations and assumptions that decision needs. This project aims to answer some of these questions in general, and to provide specific solutions In diabetes management.

  Who are we looking for?  The key requirement is competence: a master’s-level background with a high level of mathematical and computational training, for example from studies in statistics, mathematics, computer science or a nearby field, and an interest in causal inference. You should be interested in biomedical applications, ideally with some prior exposure through a thesis, a project, an internship or a collaboration, and willing to talk to and learn from clinicians and biomedical researchers about the context in which the methods will be used. Programming skills and willingness to turn methods into reusable software are expected.

   

  About the department

  The department has about 50 permanent scientific staff members, around 60 PhD students and 35 postdocs. It has strong research groups in many areas of mathematics and active PhD, postdoc, and visitors’ programs. Our buildings are located in central Copenhagen next to the central park Fælledparken. Our website https://www.math.ku.dk/english provides more information about the department and the research conducted at the department https://www.math.ku.dk/english/research/. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in a dynamic and international research environment.

  The PhD programme

  Depending on your level of education, you can undertake the PhD programme as either:

  Option A: A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree.

  Option B: An up to five year full-time study programme within the framework of the integrated MSc and PhD programme (the 3+5 scheme), if you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master´s degree – but you have an education equivalent to a Danish bachelors´s degree.

   Option A: Getting into a position on the regular PhD programme

  Qualifications needed for the regular programme To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. statistics, mathematics, or computer science. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Terms of employment in the regular programme Employment as PhD fellow is full time and for maximum 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of Science, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant with the help of the supervisor.

  Terms of appointment and payment according to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  Option B: Getting into a position on the integrated MSc and PhD programme

  Qualifications needed for the integrated MSc and PhD programme

  If you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master´s degree, you might be qualified for the integrated MSc and PhD programme, if you have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish bachelor´s degree. Here you can find out, if that is relevant for you: General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Terms of the integrated programme

  To be eligible for the integrated scholarship, you are (or are eligible to be) enrolled at one of the faculty’s master programmes.

  Students on the integrated programme will enroll as PhD students simultaneously with completing their enrollment in this MSc degree programme.

  The duration of the integrated programme is up to five years and depends on the amount of credits that you have passed on your MSc programme. For further information about the study programme, please see: www.science.ku.dk/phd, “Study Structures”.

  Until the MSc degree is obtained (when exactly two years of the full 3+5 programme remains), the grant will be paid partly in the form of up to 48 state education grant portions (in Danish: “SU-klip”) plus salary for work (teaching, supervision etc.) totalling a workload of 150 working hours per year. A PhD grant portion is currently (2026) DKK 7.426 before tax.

  When you have obtained the MSc degree, you will transfer to the salary-earning part of the scholarship for a period of two years. At that point, the terms of employment and payment will be according to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State (AC). The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

   Responsibilities and tasks:

   	
• Complete and pass the MSc education in accordance with the curriculum of the MSc programme (ONLY when you are attending the integrated MSc and PhD programme) 	
• Carry through an independent research project under supervision 	
• Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE 	
• Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad 	
• Teach and carry out knowledge dissemination activities 	
• Write scientific papers aimed at internationally recognized journals 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project 	
• Take part in the activities of both Pioneer Centres and spend time in both research environments   We are looking for candidates with the following qualifications and experience:

   	
• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD project, in particular a strong foundation in probability, statistics and/or machine learning at advanced master’s level 	
• Interest in and some exposure to biomedical applications, and willingness to work with clinicians and biomedical researchers 	
• Evidence of research ability in any form: a master’s thesis, a project, an internship or open-source work counts as much as a preprint; prior publications are not required 	
• Programming skills and interest in producing reusable, open software 	
• A curious mind-set with a strong interest in Mathematics and its applications 	
• Good English skills   Application and Assessment Procedure

  Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Please include:

   	
• Motivation letter (approximately 1.5 pages)
 	Propose your own angle on the project and argue how it fits the two groups and the wider network, including the Pioneer Centre for AI and SMARTBiomed. Tell us why this joint setup: what you expect from working across both groups that you would not get from either side alone or from an industrial machine learning lab, and how your background prepares you for it, including any experience with biomedical or other applied collaborations. 	
• Curriculum vitae (max. two pages) including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position. 	
• About you (max. one page, in prose). Tell us about the thing you are most proud of. We do not mean grades or prizes, but something you made or worked out: a report that was never published, a tool, a result, a course or side project. Say what it is and why it matters to you. Use the rest of the page for anything else you want us to know: people you have worked with, circumstances we should take into account when reading your CV, or context that does not fit a CV. 	
• Original diplomas for Bachelor or Master and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted.   How we assess

  We shortlist on the written application as a whole, weighing motivation and fit with the joint setup, the mathematical and statistical foundation relevant to the project, evidence of research ability in any form, and interest in biomedical applications. Publications are neither required nor an assessment criterion, and we do not rank applicants by the reputation of their previous institution. Selected applicants are invited to interview. Interviews may span several conversations, e.g. a technical follow-up and a conversation with the leadership of both centres. As part of this we may ask you to give a short technical presentation on a topic of your choosing, or for a sample of your work. What matters to us there is whether we can discuss science together and how we would work with each other.

  When you will be affiliated with the University of Copenhagen or otherwise have access to their research, you may be required to undergo a background screening. The purpose is to protect the security and research integrity of the University of Copenhagen.

  Application deadline

  The deadline for applications is 5 January 2027, 23:59 GMT +1.

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process

  After the deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment (shortlisted) by a committee of unbiased experts. You are notified whether you will be passed for assessment.

  An assessment committee will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the research area, skills and other requirements. The assessors will conclude whether each applicant is qualified. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process at https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

   

  Questions

  For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact the supervisors: Sebastian Weichwald (see https://sweichwald.de/#research-with-us) and Erin Gabriel (erin.gabriel@sund.ku.dk).

  General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website: https://www.science.ku.dk/phd/.

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position.

We are seeking a Financial Controller to own the integrity of Tekla’s financial reporting across the group. The Financial Controller is responsible both for meeting these obligations accurately and on time, and for building the processes, controls and automation that make them repeatable as the business scales. Key responsibilities of the role include, but are not limited to:

Financial Controlling & Reporting

• Design, implement and manage the group's balance sheet reconciliations, including building standardised templates and processes across multiple entities

• Prepare the monthly and year-end group consolidation, including intercompany eliminations, foreign currency translation and consolidated reporting packs

Tax & Trade Compliance

Financial Analysis & Performance

• Provide insightful financial analysis to support business planning, cost efficiencies and strategic priorities

• Collaborate with cross-functional teams to support business objectives

Process Improvement & Automation

• Review and implement continual improvements in Business Central, including VAT code configuration, VAT statements and financial reports

• Strengthen documentation and controls across all owned processes so they are auditable and transferable

• Strong knowledge of accounting principles, financial reporting standards and tax regulations

• Demonstrable experience of group consolidation and intercompany eliminations in a multi-entity, multi-currency environment

• Strong working knowledge of global VAT and sales tax concepts

• Exposure to packaging tax regimes is an advantage

• Experience designing and operating a balance sheet reconciliation control framework

• Confident ERP user, ideally Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central

• Demonstrable experience using AI tools such as Claude to optimise and automate financial processes and reporting, for example building reporting dashboards, automating reconciliation and compliance workflows, or analysing large transactional data sets
